all_words.explanation: A jury delivers a verdict in many trials, so the two words describe the same stage of a legal process.
A lantern is a source of light and has no connection to legal decisions.
An appeal challenges a verdict, so both words belong to the same topic of court procedure.
A tulip is a flower and is unrelated to courts or judgements.
A verdict is often described as a conviction or an acquittal, so the words are commonly used together.
A pebble is a small stone and is unrelated to legal judgements.

explanation: A verdict is the decision a jury or judge reaches at the end of a trial, which can be appealed; the associated words describe its context and outcomes, while the others belong to unrelated fields.
